rb_assessment.evidence: refresh is non-async and returns the same attempt.response to all joiners. The slot is reserved before dependency work; one timer and one handled observer attach per aggregate check. Expiry settles the response but leaves active resident; later callers neither attach raw-native observers nor dispatch checks. finish clears active only on actual aggregate native completion and exact identity. The six-group test instruments raw then attachment and proves one observer for 32 plus 128 callers; emitted-module probes independently retain the same response and native attempt after timeout.

fail sets responseSettled, marks unavailable, accounts failure/backoff once, clears the timer and resolves false before a caught advisory cancellation call. Throwing/noop cancellation cannot retain the caller promise or free the slot. Production unavailable callback only sets persistenceReady=false, so ordinary HTTP traffic is gated after timeout. This is a response deadline under a progressing JS scheduler; source comments and owning documentation explicitly exclude synchronous/native interruption.

eligible checks exact active identity, unsettled response, now < deadlineAt, fatal=false and captured invalidation generation. It runs both before prepare and immediately before synchronous publish. Tests cover 999/1000/1001ms with an unfired timer, preparation consuming the budget, and newer invalidation during check/preparation. Both generated availability catches increment persistenceInvalidationGeneration; an emitted-module pending probe cannot erase a synthetic connection failure raised through the actual generated persistenceAsync wrapper.

initializePersistenceOnce(publish=true) preserves startup defaults; recovery calls false. The entire success mutation block is guarded, including ready, probe-needed, diagnostic flags and fatal reset. Controller preparation constructs a candidate only after eligibility, then rechecks before rebinding. The aggregate awaited initializer includes entity/index/authentication schema work, and an expired attempt retains ownership through the complete finite sequential initializer. No detached or overlapping recovery pipeline is introduced. Emitted full modules prove late successful initialization leaves ready false and the prior active client identical, including the first-party authentication schema chain; fresh eligible recovery alone changes the client.

Synthetic controller timeout never enters initializer error classification. The generated initializer retains real availability/SQLite-contention classification and fatal incompatible-schema classification, including rejection after expiry. Independent full emitted-module injection of code 42703 latches fatal after a caller has already received false; subsequent readiness stays false without client publication. A real transient connection rejection returns boolean false, which the .then(healthy => finish(healthy)) observer now respects. Startup still awaits the default publishing initializer; fatal/config/auth validation precedes listener binding. No startup deadline was added or approved.

responseSettled makes failure accounting idempotent across timeout, rejection and repeated callers. Retry delay advances 250/500/1000/2000/4000/5000/5000ms, once per attempt, with monotonic cutoff. active residence takes priority over retry eligibility. Only fenced success resets delay and establishes a one-second healthy cache. Tests exercise boundaries, cap, false-check results and success reset; emitted false-initialization outcome independently remains unready before 250ms and genuinely recovers at eligibility. Late completion cannot count failure twice or establish healthy cache. Existing mixed-cutoff response semantics remain intact.

independent_checks.command: bun --no-install --env-file=/dev/null run - (inline in-memory evaluation of both complete generated persistence modules with synthetic native SQL and monotonic timers)
independent_checks.method: Read each pinned generated module, remove its two native import statements and export markers, substitute a fixed module URL, transpile TypeScript with Bun.Transpiler and evaluate the complete module in AsyncFunction. Supply a callable synthetic SQL handle, captured deferred query, deterministic performance.now/setTimeout/clearTimeout, test-only state accessors and captured diagnostics. The generated startup initializer, recovery initializer, persistenceAsync classifier, first-party schema setup, controller and active-client proxy publication run as emitted. Assertions compare original active-client object identity, ready/fatal/probe-needed/generation, response identity, native call counts, retry eligibility and timer cleanup. No generated product file was edited; the module URL substitution only enables isolated evaluation.
independent_checks.limits: Synthetic asynchronous SQL outcomes and logical time, not live PostgreSQL or a measured wall-clock latency bound. Module startup succeeds under mocks before each fault is injected. Native connection construction stayed one per module; this does not mean the schema pipeline issues only one SQL statement. The retained bound is one aggregate readiness attempt, not all ordinary application database traffic.
